name: Exp E: State-change thumbnail (What to Eat, plus Strength as a second test)
hypothesis: Our two most-shown practical videos have a packaging problem, not a discovery problem. A state-change thumbnail of 4 words or fewer that keeps the question lifts CTR toward 3.8–4.7%.
change: Only the thumbnail changes, with no body imagery. What to Eat was swapped around 11-04 and Strength on 11-10. No other edits to either video until 11-24, including description links and end screens.
metric: CTR on impressions after the swap vs CTR just before it (What to Eat about 1.9%, Strength about 0.6%), with views per day not falling. Success: 3.0%+ on both.
min_sample: 1,000 new impressions or 14 days per video, whichever comes later (read on 11-24)
result: Not readable yet. What to Eat moved only from about 790 to 797 lifetime minutes this week. Strength is still earning a little. Read on 11-24 against the before-swap rate, not the overall average.

name: Exp F: A benefit-framed subscribe line in Shorts
hypothesis: One honest line that names the channel's promise will at least double how often Shorts viewers subscribe.
change: The 08:00 and 13:00 Shorts ended with 'We answer one tirzepatide question from the research every day. Subscribe if that helps.' The 20:00 Shorts were the control.
metric: Subscribers per 1,000 views at day 7, line vs control, and channel subscribers per day vs the 1.3-a-day baseline. Success: 2× the control and 2.5+ a day.
result: Lost. Channel subscribers went from 382 (11-03) to 386 (11-16): about 0.3 a day, against a 1.3 baseline and a 2.5 target. Every Short with per-Short data shows 0 subscribers, with or without the line. The last day can't change the result. This is confounded by Shorts views falling to about half the baseline, but nothing points to a lift. The line comes out from 11-17, when the owner's new Shorts ending takes over.

name: Exp G: Studio related-video link on top Shorts
hypothesis: The related-video link is the only clickable path from a Short. Setting it on our best body and pen Shorts, aimed at the long video on the same topic, will create Shorts traffic to long videos that converts to subscribers.
change:
The owner sets one related-video link per Short, with targets matched by topic:
- hair grow-back (1,025) and hair in women (119) → Hair Loss
- injection site (254), injection sites (202), pen blood (111) and pen out of the fridge (11-15) → Pen how-to
- nausea (190) → Side Effects
- bones (249) → Bones & Muscle
- breakfast (134) → What to Eat
- Thanksgiving (11-06) → Thanksgiving
No other change to these Shorts.
metric: Views and minutes from Shorts on each target long video in the 7 days after the link is set, vs 0 before. Success: at least 1 long-video view per 100 new Short views across the set, plus a visible rise in channel subscribers.
min_sample: 8 linked Shorts, 7 days after the links are set
result: Not started. The links still aren't set after 7 days, and views from Shorts are still 0 on every long video. The targets were updated now that the Hair Loss and Pen long videos are live; the test starts the day the owner sets the links.

name: Exp H: Second payoff at 15–30 s in long-form scripts
hypothesis: The biggest drop comes at 12–35 s (14 of 19 curves), right after the first answer. A second concrete payoff (a number or the first step) at 15–30 s, with an open loop of one sentence at most, lifts the 30-second hold and the midpoint hold.
change: Every long video from the 11-11 Pen video onward uses this structure. Nothing else in the script template changes.
metric: Day-7 median hold at 30 s and median relative hold at the midpoint, vs the n=19 baseline (30-second hold about 77%, midpoint 43.6). Success: 30-second hold of 82%+ and midpoint of 48+.
min_sample: 6 long videos built this way, at day 7
result: Started on 11-11. Pen is read on 11-18 and Alcohol on 11-19. Early anecdote: average view percentage of 63% for Pen and 67% for Alcohol at days 3–4, against a long-form norm of about 45%. Too few and too early to judge.

name: short-length (owner): tight vs standard Shorts
hypothesis: Tighter Shorts (90–120 words, 40–55 s) earn more views and a higher average view percentage than standard ones (135–160 words, 65–80 s).
change: Each Short's task sets `tight` or `standard`, alternating by slot and day, from 11-12 to 11-26.
metric: Median views and average view percentage per arm at day 7.
min_sample: All Shorts from 11-12 to 11-26 (about 20 per arm), each at day 7
result: No read until 11-26. Record the winner in the playbook then.

name: hook-archetype (owner): opening style for Shorts
hypothesis: Some of the 5 opening styles (result-first, negation, number-first, myth-flip, recognition-question) beat the others on views and average view percentage.
metric: Median views and average view percentage per style at day 7.
result: No style has n≥8 yet. Don't read it.

name: Search-demand long videos vs Lane A (owner)
hypothesis: Device how-to, what-to-expect, label-change and approved-drug head-to-head long videos bring more search views and minutes than Lane A videos of the same age.
change: 2–3 of the week's long videos are search-demand videos, starting with Pen (11-11) and First Month (11-13). This week: Mounjaro vs Zepbound, Foundayo What to Expect, Zepbound Vial vs Pen.
metric: Minutes and search views at day 14, matched by age.
result: Too early. Anecdote: Pen had 22 min on 17 views at day 4, and 8 of its 12 non-subscriber views came from search. Search pulls in viewers, but the volume is small so far. First readouts: Pen on 11-25, First Month on 11-27.
